deepdive.sec: Indian Alcobev / Premium & Above IMFL Consolidation

bull_bear.body: Priority on debt reduction (Net Debt/EBITDA <1.0x by FY29); Dividend recommended INR 1/share; Deferred consideration of EUR 28 Mn payable to Pernod Ricard after 4 years; Working capital cycle targeted at 53-55 days.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical tension driving raw material inflation; Delay in TSMA transition for remaining 3 states (target full exit by FY27 end); Regulatory uncertainty on excise policies (Telangana dues outstanding); Integration execution risk in non-southern markets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and operationally focused; emphasized 'record volumes' post-TSMA exit disruptions; transparent on accounting changes; cautious on Q1 margin pressure due to inflation but firm on full-year guidance.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The accounting reclassification of selling expenses creates a false impression of margin expansion (EBITDA margin up) while actually compressing the top-line; the INR 63 Cr exceptional charge masks underlying operational profitability; TSMA fees will drop from ~INR 63 Cr (Q4 impact) to INR 55-60 Cr full year FY27 as transition completes.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet as at Jun-26: Total Gross Debt INR 2,241 cr (Term Loan 2,041, Working Capital Loan 175, Others 25) versus INR 2,295 cr at Mar-26; Total Net Debt INR 2,100 cr at Jun-26 versus INR 1,911 cr at Mar-26, with cash & equivalents of INR 141 cr versus INR 384 cr.
- Term loan structure: 'a period of 6 years of which the initial 2 years have a principal moratorium', 'a balloon repayment structure, with 65% of the principal repayment to be made in the 6th year', and 'effective interest rate on the above term loan is ~10%-11%'; lenders shown as Banks, NBFCs and Others.
- Stated deleveraging intent: the rise in net debt from Mar-26 to Jun-26 is attributed to 'complete working capital-cycle investment', with 'Target Net Debt for Mar-27 below Mar-26 levels'.
- Equity funding history: '2018 – 2024: Restructuring of debt with EARC and one-time settlements', 'Raised ₹ 310 crs+ via pref issues', 'Achieved net debt free status'; preferential issues of INR 126 crores (Dec-21, Lotus Family Trust/Promoter Group), INR 85 crores (Jun-22, Channel Partners) and INR 100 crores (Dec-22, Think Investments), plus a 2025 preferential issue with Promoter Group, Axana Estates and QRG Investments among investors.
- Reinvestment is going into minority stakes in premium adjacencies: a follow-on investment of INR 2 crores (primary infusion) into Bartisans under the heading 'Stake Increase', with stakes of 41.45% and 36.17% (fully diluted basis) shown; the extraction does not bind which figure is pre- versus post-investment. Capital is earmarked for Q-commerce expansion, collaborative launches and product innovation including single-serve formats.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Imperial Blue contributed 4.6 Mn cases in Q4 (total 8 Mn+); Ex-IB volumes grew 14% in FY26 to 13.6 Mn cases; Mansion House crossed 10 Mn cases benchmark; IB seasonality is flatter than TI legacy (H2 ~52% of vol).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- 'Largest domestic Prestige & Above (P&A) IMFL player and third-largest P&A IMFL player in India'; also 'Largest P&A IMFL Player in South-India'.
- 'Largest P&A player in South India with ~40% market share (ex-Tamil Nadu)'.
- Brand claims stated verbatim: 'Mansion House is the highest selling & fastest growing premium brandy in the World' and 'Imperial Blue is the 3rd largest whisky Globally' (source: 'Media Reports, Management Estimates'). The accompanying badge grid of ordinals (1st/2nd/3rd/7th/8th) loses its label-to-value binding in extraction, so the individual rankings are not asserted here.
- 'Highest Selling Deluxe Whisky in Jun-26' is claimed for the portfolio in the Q1 FY27 header strip.
- Two years ago the company describes itself as a '2-brand and 1-category player' with '90%+ volume saliency from Brandy' and '85%+ volume saliency from Southern India'; the stated journey ahead is a 'Pan-India Player with 2 of the largest brands in 2 of the largest IMFL Categories' with '65%+ and 30%+ volume saliency from Whisky and Brandy respectively' (data for LTM Mar-26).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Imperial Blue was acquired from a third party with the acquisition 'completed in Nov-25' (hence YoY growth 'not applicable' for IB); integration is 'substantially completed' with one state left under the Transition Services and Manufacturing Agreement (TSMA), max exit Q4 FY27.
- [Regulation] 'The India-UK Free Trade Agreement came into effect in mid-July' with reduced Scotch import costs expected in financials from Q3 FY27; 'Karnataka – one of the largest markets for both IB and MHB, is witnessing strong growth on the back of the recent excise policy reforms'.
- [Accounting change] From Q4 FY26 onwards selling expenses (discounts, schemes and similar incentives) move from Other Expense to a reduction from Gross Revenue; the deck's illustration shows GP margin falling from 50% to 44% and EBITDA margin rising from 15% to 17% with 'No Change' to EBITDA — made because the business expanded into non-corporation market states after the IB acquisition.
- [Associate/Investee] Spaceman Spirits Lab (SSL) 'clocks 2.2x volume over Q1 FY26'; SSL brands are being launched in TI strongholds under a 'Usership Agreement' across Southern, Northern, Eastern and North-Eastern markets over FY27.
- [Brand marketing] New Imperial Blue theme communication rolled out across 'nearly 28,000 on-trade and off-trade outlets nationwide', with long-term tie-ups signed with 82.5 Grey, Essence Media, Dentsu Isobar and Apostrophe.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Current Q4 margin 15.5% (adj); Path to 16-18% via: 60-100 bps from India-UK FTA (custom duty on Scotch); Supply chain synergies (bottling cost savings INR 10 Cr/yr from Prag expansion); Operating leverage; Potential price hikes in Telangana. Risks: Geopolitical input cost inflation.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Volume Growth: High-single to low-double digit for FY27, double-digit CAGR over 3 years; Margin: 16%-18% EBITDA over 24-36 months; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex: Maintenance only (~INR 25 Cr/year for FY27-28).

outlook.body: Not applicable for FMCG/Alcobev sector; focus is on volume throughput and distribution reach.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Pan-India expansion of legacy brands (Mansion House) into North/West markets in FY27; Luxury portfolio expansion via Spaceman Spirits Lab (Monarch, Amara Vodka); Nigeria subsidiary investment (INR 30 Cr) to capture 2.5 Lakh case opportunity.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Tilaknagar reported a transformative Q4FY26 with 135% volume growth driven by the first full quarter of Imperial Blue, though reported revenue margins compressed due to a strategic accounting change netting selling expenses against revenue. The core thesis hinges on successful integration (75% TSMA exit achieved), targeting 16-18% EBITDA margins via synergies and cost optimization, while guiding net debt/EBITDA below 1.0x by FY29.
